definition: HLM stands for Hierarchical Linear Modeling, a statistical research method used to examine factors operating at more than one level at the same time, such as within-person and between-person influences. In this context, it helps analyze cross-level relationships in questionnaire data.

reasons: The packet does not explicitly define HLM as a “statistical research method,” only that the study “employs Hierarchical Linear Modeling (HLM) as the research tool.”

The definition claims HLM examines “factors operating at more than one level at the same time”; the packet mentions a “cross-level design” but does not state simultaneous operation “at the same time.”

The definition says it helps analyze “cross-level relationships in questionnaire data”; the packet supports use in a questionnaire-based cross-level design, but it does not explicitly describe HLM as analyzing “cross-level relationships.”
The definition uses the phrasing “within-person and between-person influences,” while the packet specifies “within-individual and between-individual levels,” which is not the same wording.
